accepted.question_text: In recovery problems with noisy data, why do semidefinite-programming relaxations of maximum-likelihood estimators often remain tight beyond the exact-recovery regime? More concretely, when noise is large enough that the maximum-likelihood estimator cannot exactly recover the ground truth, under what structural or probabilistic conditions does the SDP relaxation still return a solution that lies in the original nonconvex model class, or equivalently matches the lower-rank quasi-maximum-likelihood solution instead of requiring a rounding step?

evidence.quote: We have observed an interesting, yet unexplained, phenomenon: Semidefinite programming (SDP) based relaxations of maximum likelihood estimators (MLE) tend to be tight in recovery problems with noisy data, even when MLE cannot exactly recover the ground truth.
However, to the best of our knowledge, their tightness is not understood beyond this regime.
Yet, to the best of our knowledge, there is no theoretical understanding of this rank recovery phenomenon.

accepted.question_text: Let d > 1, n > 2, and m >= d + 1. Let A in R^(d x m) be a point cloud whose m columns are random points in R^d with i.i.d. uniform coordinates in [0,1]^d, and let O_1, ..., O_n be orthogonal transformations in R^d. Suppose the observed data are matrices A_i = O_i A + sigma eta_i in R^(d x m), where each eta_i has i.i.d. standard Gaussian entries. Form the generalized orthogonal Procrustes quasi-maximum-likelihood problem of maximizing Tr(CX) over block matrices X with X >= 0, X_ii = I_(d x d), and rank(X) <= d, and its semidefinite relaxation obtained by dropping the rank constraint. Does there exist a threshold sigma* > 0 such that whenever sigma < sigma*, with high probability the SDP relaxation has rank d and therefore exactly matches the quasi-maximum-likelihood solution?

evidence.quote: We focus on a particular type of convex relaxations, namely semidefinite programming (SDP) based relaxations, and illustrate both these techniques and the open problem we wish to pose via the generalized orthogonal Procrustes problem (Nemirovski (2007)): There is an unknown underlying point cloud of m points in R d, A in R d×m (where columns of A represent the coordinates of the points) and n unknown orthogonal transformations in R d, {Oi} n i=1 satisfying OiOT i = Id×d. We are given n noisy measurements of the form Ai = OiA+ση, and, for simplicity, assume the noise to be white Gaussian.
The semidefinite relaxation in Bandeira et al. (2013) can then be obtained by dropping the non-convex rank constraint, giving the following SDP max Tr(CX) subject to X >= 0, forall_i Xii = Id×d.

needs_review.question_text_raw: Below a certain noise level the solution to SDP-based relaxation in Bandeira et al. (2014) has rank d, thus matching the quasi-MLE.

evidence.quote: The multireference alignment consists in estimating a d-dimensional signal by observing n shifted noisy copies of it. For the sake of brevity, we will not describe the problem or the SDP based relaxation here (and refer the reader to Bandeira et al. (2014)) but take the opportunity to conjecture that a similar phenomenon happens: Below a certain noise level the solution to SDP-based relaxation in Bandeira et al. (2014) has rank d, thus matching the quasi-MLE.
Although not going into details, we note that the SDP for this problem is considerably different than (3), in particular, it has Omega(n^2 d^2) positivity constraints.
